summary: A public statement by Public Key Partners about public key standards and licenses. It is informational only and not an Internet standard.

eli5.summary: A company explains who may use its secret-code ideas and under what rules.

questions: what patents cover public key cryptography
subtitle: Public Key Partners' statement on patent licensing for cryptography

tldr.problem: Public Key Partners held exclusive sublicensing rights to foundational public-key cryptography patents, and the industry needed to know the terms under which they would grant licenses.
tldr.mechanism: Public Key Partners issued a public statement assuring that they would license patents for RSA digital signatures under reasonable terms on a non-discriminatory basis, in compliance with standards bodies like ANSI and IEEE.
tldr.outcome: This statement was significant for the adoption of RSA as a digital signature standard. It clarified that the patent holders would not block the use of public-key cryptography in open standards.

today: RFC 1170 is Informational. It documents Public Key Partners' licensing stance as of January 1991. The underlying patents have since expired, and public-key cryptography is now widely standardized and deployed throughout the Internet.

sections.title: The Patents
sections.content:
Public Key Partners held exclusive sublicensing rights to four foundational public-key cryptography patents, granted by MIT and Stanford:

  • Diffie-Hellman (U.S. Patent 4,200,770): key exchange
  • Hellman-Merkle (U.S. Patent 4,218,582): public-key encryption
  • RSA (U.S. Patent 4,405,829): encryption and digital signatures
  • Hellman-Pohlig (U.S. Patent 4,424,414): exponential cryptography

The RFC states that these patents cover all known methods of practicing public-key cryptography, including variations known as El Gamal.
sections.eli5: The company owned the rights to four big ideas about how to make secret codes that are safe to share.

sections.title: Licensing Terms
sections.content:
Public Key Partners endorsed the use of RSA in a digital signature standard and gave its assurance that licenses would be made available under reasonable terms and conditions on a non-discriminatory basis. This commitment aligned with the policies of ANSI and the IEEE, ensuring that the standards bodies could adopt RSA without concern that patent holders would restrict access.

The statement was intended to remove barriers to the adoption of public-key cryptography in open standards and commercial products.
sections.eli5: The company promised not to block anyone from using these ideas, and to charge fair prices that everyone pays.

sections.title: Significance for Open Standards
sections.content:
This statement was important because it addressed a real concern: without assurance of reasonable licensing terms, standards organizations might avoid technologies covered by restrictive patents. By publicly committing to fair licensing, Public Key Partners helped clear the way for RSA and other public-key methods to become part of Internet standards.

The RFC thanks all those who worked to make the technology available for commercial use.
sections.eli5: This promise helped the Internet community use these code-making ideas without worrying they would be blocked.
